title: ENG-205 Beowulf Part 2 — 4 Main Ideas
subject: ENG-205
topic: Beowulf Part 2 (Another Attack to Another Celebration at Heorot)

cards.term: What happens in the section Another Attack
cards.def: While the Danes slept after the feast, Grendel's mother broke into Heorot, seized Aeschere, took back Grendel's arm, and fled to the fen.

cards.term: Why Beowulf is absent during the attack
cards.def: Beowulf had been given a different lodging after the treasure-giving, so he was not sleeping in Heorot when she came.

cards.term: How Grendel's mother compares to Grendel
cards.def: The poet says her attack was less terrible than Grendel's only in the way that a woman warrior is less fearsome than an armed man.
Hrothgar answers Beowulf's greeting with "Rest? What is rest? Sorrow has returned," and mourns Aeschere as his dearest friend.
Hrothgar describes a lake where the water burns at night and a hunted stag would rather die than dive in, to show how dangerous it is.
Beowulf tells Hrothgar that it is better to avenge a friend than to mourn, because every man should win glory before he dies.
Hrothgar and Beowulf followed the monster's tracks over cliffs and narrow paths until they found Aeschere's head at the foot of a cliff.
Beowulf put on his mail shirt and boar-crested helmet and took Hrunting, the sword Unferth lent him.
Beowulf asked Hrothgar to care for his men and send his treasures to Hygelac if he died, and he left his own sword to Unferth.
Grendel's mother seized Beowulf and dragged him to her underwater hall, while sea-beasts tore at his mail shirt on the way down.
Hrunting rang against Grendel's mother's head but would not bite, the first time the famous blade ever failed.
When the sword failed, Beowulf flung it aside and wrestled her with his bare hands, because a man seeking lasting glory must rely on his own strength.

cards.term: How the mail shirt saves Beowulf
cards.def: When Grendel's mother pinned Beowulf and stabbed with her knife, his chain-mail turned the blade, and God granted him victory.
Beowulf saw an ancient giant-made sword hanging in her hall and swung it through her neck.
Beowulf cut off the dead Grendel's head to take revenge for all the Danes whom Grendel had killed.
The blade melted like ice because Grendel's blood was so hot and poisonous, leaving only the hilt.

cards.term: The Danes give up on Beowulf
cards.def: When blood surged up in the mere, the Danes assumed Beowulf was dead and went home, but the Geats waited loyally.

cards.term: What Beowulf brings back from the mere
cards.def: Beowulf left the rest of the treasure behind and brought back only Grendel's head and the golden hilt of the giant sword.

cards.term: What happens in the section Another Celebration at Heorot
cards.def: Beowulf presented Grendel's head, told of the underwater fight, and gave Hrothgar the golden hilt, and a new feast restored joy to the hall.
The hilt is engraved with the story of how God destroyed the giants in the flood, and runes on it name the man it was made for.
Hrothgar warns Beowulf that a powerful man who grows proud and stingy will be struck down, so he should choose eternal rewards instead.
Hrothgar reminds Beowulf that his strength will soon fade through sickness, the sword, fire, water, or old age.

cards.term: Why Hrothgar tells the story of Heremod
cards.def: Hrothgar tells of Heremod, who killed his comrades and stopped giving rings, as an example of the king Beowulf must not become.
Before leaving, Beowulf returned Hrunting to Unferth, thanked him, and did not blame the sword for failing.
Beowulf promises Hrothgar that he will come with an army if enemies threaten Denmark, and he invites Hrethric to visit the Geats.
Hrothgar predicts that if Hygelac dies, the Geats could find no better king than Beowulf.

cards.term: How Beowulf has united two peoples
cards.def: Hrothgar says Beowulf has brought the Geats and the Danes into peace, so gifts will now pass between them across the sea.
Hrothgar kissed and embraced Beowulf and wept, because he sensed that they would never meet again.
Hrunting fails and the giant sword melts, which suggests that Beowulf's victories depend on his own strength and God's help rather than on weapons.

cards.term: Grendel's mother as the cycle of war
cards.def: Grendel's mother stands for the recurring cycle of war, because her revenge for Grendel provokes Beowulf's revenge for Aeschere in turn.
The joyful feast is followed by Grendel's mother's night attack and then by the light that fills her hall when she dies and the new feast in Heorot.
As Beowulf leaves Denmark, the narrator foretells that Hrothgar will remain a peerless king only until old age saps his strength.
Old Hrothgar's sermon warns young Beowulf that his strength will fade, which sets up the old king Beowulf will become.
